To find the physical dimension of the constant $k$, we start with the given relationship:
$$\text{Speed} = k \times \text{Duration}$$

We know the dimensions of speed and duration:
- The dimension of Speed is $\frac{\text{Length}}{\text{Time}}$ (L/T).
- The dimension of Duration is $\text{Time}$ (T).

For the equation to be dimensionally consistent, the dimensions on both sides must be equal:
$$[\text{Speed}] = [k] \times [\text{Duration}]$$
$$\frac{\text{Length}}{\text{Time}} = [k] \times \text{Time}$$

Now, we solve for the dimension of $k$:
$$[k] = \frac{[\text{Speed}]}{[\text{Duration}]} = \frac{\text{Length} / \text{Time}}{\text{Time}}$$
$$[k] = \frac{\text{Length}}{\text{Time}^2}$$

The physical dimension of the constant $k$ is Length divided by Time squared.

<ANSWER>Length / Time^2</ANSWER>
